title: Billet Designator-Barracks and Grounds Marine (GySgt to Pvt) FMOS*, DC I&L
raw_text:
3. MOS 8911, Billet Designator-Barracks and Grounds Marine (GySgt to Pvt)
FMOS*, DC I&L

    a. Summary. Barracks and Grounds Marines supervise the policing and
minor maintenance of barracks and grounds; supervise or assist in the
supervision of, training, routine administration; and employment of units.

       b.    Prerequisites.       See requirements.

       c.    Requirements

             (1) Not to be assigned to personnel either as a primary or additional
MOS.

             (2) To be used only as a billet designator in T/O's.

       d.    Duties

        (1) Supervises working parties in maintaining barracks, buildings,
and grounds in a clean, sanitary, and orderly condition.

        (2) Makes periodic inspections of plumbing, electrical equipment, and
other building components and arranges for required repairs.

        (3) Maintains a stock of tools, equipment, and housekeeping gear to
supply working parties.

             (4) Services buildings and materials such as light bulbs and towels.

        (5) Performs preventive maintenance and makes minor repairs to tools
and equipment.



                                              3-507                   Enclosure (1)
 3156                                                                NAVMC 1200.1L



            (6) Requisitions supplies and equipment.

        (7) Accompanies inspecting officer on tours of inspection and
prepares reports pertaining to unsanitary or faulty conditions.

        (8) Assists in the supervision of a unit engaged in enforcing
military regulations and guarding lives and property at a military
installation.

            (9) Inspects and determines condition of unit weapons and equipment.

            (10) Initiates action to correct deficiencies.

        (11) Supervises preparation of unit correspondence, reports,
schedules, and rosters.

        (12) Organizes and supervises the necessary housekeeping functions
within the organization.

        (13) Conducts or supervises subordinates conducting training in
military subjects.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Residential Advisors 39-9041.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.

The Command Senior Enlisted Leader Occupational Field is comprised of the following two specialties: 8991, Sergeant Major of the Marine Corps and 8999, Sergeant Major-First Sergeant. Both specialties serve as the command senior enlisted leader, responsible to the commander for all matters that influence the readiness, effectiveness, and performance of the command. They are the institutional advocates of the organization’s history, traditions, customs, and courtesies and enlisted career human resource development. The Command Senior Enlisted Leader assists with communicating and enforcing the commander’s intent and guidance.

(2) Makes periodic inspections of plumbing, electrical equipment, and other building components and arranges for required repairs. (3) Maintains a stock of tools, equipment, and housekeeping gear to supply working parties. (4) Services buildings and materials such as light bulbs and towels. (5) Performs preventive maintenance and makes minor repairs to tools and equipment. (6) Requisitions supplies and equipment. (7) Accompanies inspecting officer on tours of inspection and prepares reports pertaining to unsanitary or faulty conditions. nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
